items.text: A builder finds soft organic topsoil at footing depth. What does the MRC require?

B. Bear the footing on undisturbed natural soil or engineered fill - never organic or uncompacted fill — R401.2/R401.3 require footings to bear on undisturbed natural soil or engineered fill, never on organic soil, uncompacted fill, or frozen soil.
What presumptive load-bearing value does the MRC assign to sandy gravel (GW, GP)?
C. 3,000 psf — Table R401.4.1: sandy gravel/gravel = 3,000 psf; sand-class soils = 2,000, clays = 1,500, sedimentary rock = 4,000.
Which soil carries the highest presumptive load-bearing value in the MRC table?
A. Crystalline bedrock at 12,000 psf — Table R401.4.1 tops out at crystalline bedrock, 12,000 psf; sedimentary/foliated rock is 4,000 psf.
What is the minimum footing thickness under the MRC?
D. 6 inches — R403.1.1 sets the minimum footing thickness at 6 inches.
A footing runs along ground that drops steeply. What is the maximum slope of the footing bottom before stepped footings are required?
B. 1 in 10, or 10 percent — R403.1.5 - top of footing level, bottom slope maximum 1 in 10 (10 percent); steeper terrain requires stepped footings.
Building next to a hillside, at what slope steepness do the MRC clearance and setback provisions kick in?

C. Steeper than 1 vertical in 3 horizontal, about 33 percent — R403.1.7 triggers slope clearance/setback rules for placement on or adjacent to slopes steeper than 1 vertical in 3 horizontal (33.3 percent); 1-in-2 is the trap.
Which structure is exempt from frost-depth footing requirements?

B. A freestanding light-frame accessory building of 600 square feet or less with eave height 10 feet or less — R403.1.4.1 exempts freestanding accessory buildings up to 600 sq ft light-frame (400 sq ft other construction) with eave height 10 ft or less, and decks not supported by a dwelling.
A house has brick veneer. How far must the foundation wall extend above finished grade?
D. 4 inches — R404.1.6 - minimum 4 inches above finished grade where masonry veneer is used, 6 inches elsewhere.
When may a crew backfill against a new poured-concrete basement wall?

A. After the wall has cured to sufficient strength and is anchored to the floor above or braced — R404.1.7 - do not backfill until the wall has cured to sufficient strength and is anchored to the floor above or braced.
How should foundation backfill be placed?
A. Clean material in 6 to 12 inch compacted lifts — Backfill in 6-12 inch compacted lifts of clean material - no organics, frozen chunks, or large rock (R404.1.7 practice).
Where must a foundation perimeter drain be installed relative to the footing?

C. At or below the top of the footing, discharging by gravity or mechanical means — R405.1 requires drains at or below the top of the footing (or below bottom of slab), discharging by gravity or mechanical means into an approved system.
For a gravel foundation drain, how far must the gravel extend beyond and above the footing?

B. 1 foot beyond the outside edge of the footing and 6 inches above its top, with a filter membrane — R405.1 - gravel extends 1 foot beyond the outside edge of the footing and 6 inches above its top, covered with an approved filter membrane; swapping the two numbers is the listed trap.
A basement is built in well-drained sand-gravel soils (Group I). What foundation drainage is required?
D. None - the drainage system exception applies to well-drained Group I soils — R405.1 exception: no drainage system required on well-drained ground or sand-gravel mixture soils (USCS Group I).
How is a masonry foundation wall dampproofed under the MRC default method?

B. Three-eighths inch portland cement parging, then a bituminous coating, from top of footing to finished grade — R406.1 - masonry walls get 3/8-inch portland cement parging then bituminous coating, applied from top of footing to finished grade; the membrane lists are R406.2 waterproofing materials.
What minimum 28-day strength is required for footings and interior slabs in Michigan?
A. 2,500 psi — Table R402.2 (severe weathering): footings, basement walls not exposed to weather, and interior slabs = 2,500 psi.
A poured concrete wall will be exposed to the weather. What minimum strength applies?
C. 3,000 psi — Table R402.2: vertical concrete exposed to weather = 3,000 psi; 2,500 is the unexposed value and 3,500 is the garage/porch slab value.
Why must calcium chloride accelerator be avoided in concrete with embedded steel?

B. It promotes corrosion of the steel - use a non-chloride accelerator instead — Calcium chloride promotes corrosion of embedded/prestressed steel; the corpus specifies non-chloride accelerators instead.
What is the diameter of a number 4 rebar?
D. One-half inch — Rebar sizes are eighths of an inch: #4 = 4/8 = 1/2 inch (#3 = 3/8, #5 = 5/8).
How much concrete cover is required over rebar cast directly against earth?
C. 3 inches — ACI 318 practice (per corpus): 3-inch cover where concrete is cast against earth.
Where should footing rebar and slab welded-wire mesh each be positioned?

A. Footing rebar in the bottom third; slab mesh in the upper third, chaired up — Footing rebar goes in the bottom third (tension zone); slab mesh in the upper third - mesh left on the ground does nothing (corpus section 5).
During finishing, bleed water appears on the slab surface. What is correct practice?
C. Wait for the bleed water to evaporate before continuing finishing — The finishing sequence requires waiting out bleed water - never finishing it into the surface (corpus section 5).
How deep must a control joint be cut in a 4-inch slab?
D. At least 1 inch - one-quarter of the slab depth — Control/contraction joints are cut at least 1/4 of slab depth: 4 inches x 1/4 = 1 inch (corpus section 5).
About what fraction of its design strength does properly cured concrete reach at 7 days?
D. About 70 percent, with full design strength at 28 days — ACI practice per corpus: 7 days is about 70 percent of design strength; full design strength at 28 days.
In cold weather, freshly placed concrete must be protected from freezing until it reaches what strength?
A. 500 psi — Cold-weather practice: protect from freezing until concrete reaches 500 psi, roughly the first 48-72 hours (corpus section 5).
What are the MRC minimums for an interior slab on grade: thickness, granular base, and vapor retarder?

B. 3 and one-half inch slab, 4 inch approved granular base, 6-mil polyethylene lapped 6 inches — R506 - minimum 3.5-inch slab, 4-inch approved granular base, and 6-mil polyethylene vapor retarder with joints lapped 6 inches.
A garage slab measures 18 feet by 36 feet at 6 inches thick. How many cubic yards of concrete does it take?
C. 12 cubic yards — Cubic yards = L x W x T (ft) / 27: 18 x 36 x 0.5 = 324 cubic feet / 27 = 12 CY (order about 10 percent extra).
What slump range is typical for residential concrete flatwork?
D. 4 to 6 inches — Typical residential slump is 4-6 inches (footings often 2-4); the slump test measures workability (corpus section 5).
A builder will disturb 1.5 acres of soil, far from any waterway. What Michigan permit applies?

A. A soil erosion (SESC) permit under Part 91 of NREPA - triggered at 1 acre or within 500 feet of a lake or stream — Part 91 of NREPA (1994 PA 451) requires an SESC permit for earth disturbance of 1 acre or more OR within 500 feet of a lake or stream; wetlands are Part 303, the classic trap.
A trench in Type C soil must be protected. Which method is NOT allowed?
B. Benching the excavation walls — Type C soil cannot be benched - only sloping (1.5H:1V) or shielding/shoring is permitted (Part 9/Subpart P).
A benchmark elevation is 100.00 feet. The backsight rod reads 4.50 and the foresight on the footing corner reads 6.20. What is the footing corner elevation?
D. 98.30 feet — HI = benchmark + backsight = 100.00 + 4.50 = 104.50; point elevation = HI - foresight = 104.50 - 6.20 = 98.30 (corpus section 8 leveling math).
